concepts.label: Covering index
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - promoted. This page is the definitional source: it is the relational property that holds between an index and a query, not a kind of index, and the page says so ('An index, in this case, is called a covering index'), i.e. the same index is or is not covering depending on the query.

concepts.label: Covered query
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the page names this as a separate term in the same sentence as the covering index ('the query is called a covered query'), and it is the other end of the same relation. Nothing in the corpus names it, although index:covering-index is promoted. Phase 2 may prefer to fold it into index:covering-index as the query-side alias; I have kept it separate because the plan-field evidence attaches to the query, not to the index.

relations.subject: index:covering-index
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - the defining property is stated negatively: the fetch step does not happen. Recorded with doesNotSupport rather than a minted predicate because the page's whole claim is the absence of the data-service fetch.
relations.evidence: When an index includes the actual values of all the fields specified in the query, the index covers the query and does not require an additional step to fetch the actual values from the data service. An index, in this case, is called a covering index and the query is called a covered query. As a result, covered queries are faster and deliver better performance.

relations.subject: index:covered-query
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - the query side of the same definitional sentence
relations.evidence: If we select `state` from the `hotel` keyspace, the actual values of the field `state` that are to be returned are present in the index `idx_state`, and avoids an additional step to fetch the data. In this case, the index `idx_state` is called a covering index and the query is a covered query.

relations.subject: index:covering-index
relations.evidence: To see details of covering indexes at work, you can view the query execution plan using the EXPLAIN statement. When a query uses a covering index, the EXPLAIN statement shows that a covering index is used for data access, thus avoiding the overhead associated with key-value document fetches.

relations.subject: index:covering-index
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - the MISSING rule is a hard qualification condition, not a preference: the query must exclude MISSING for the index to qualify
relations.evidence: `MISSING` items are not indexed by indexers. To take advantage of covering indexes and for the index to qualify, a query needs to exclude documents where the index key expression evaluates to `MISSING`.

relations.subject: index:covering-index
relations.evidence: Covering indexes are applicable to secondary index scans and can be used with global secondary indexes (GSI). Queries with expressions and aggregates benefit from covering indexes.

relations.subject: index:covering-index

relations.evidence: You cannot use multiple GSI indexes to cover a query. You must create a composite index with all the required fields for the query engine to cover by GSI and not require reading the documents from the data nodes.

notable_absence.finding: This is the only page of the four cross-linked performance pages whose Related Links omit early-filters-and-pagination.md. index_pushdowns.md, groupby-aggregate-performance.md and early-filters-and-pagination.md all carry the full set of four; covering-indexes.md carries three. The omission matters more here than anywhere else, because early-filters-and-pagination.md is written as the direct continuation of this page - its lede is 'When covering indexes and index pushdowns are not available...' and its whole explanatory device is that _index_key/index_conditions/index_keys are analogous to this page's cover/filter_covers/covers. So the page a reader of covering-indexes.md most needs next is the one link it lacks. A second absence: the page never states which index types CANNOT cover a query, only that secondary and GSI can, so there is no evidence here for a doesNotSupport relation to index-type:primary-index or index-type:view even though the restriction to 'secondary index scans' implies one.

cross_component_finding: The page teaches covering indexes entirely through two EXPLAIN plan fields - `covers` and `filter_covers` - and never names them in prose, only in code blocks and callout-table rows ('The covers object shows details of the data covered by the index'). That makes the ontology's hook into this page the plan field rather than the concept, and it is why index:covers-plan-field already exists at the extraction layer while its sibling filter_covers did not. Three of the five pages in this batch (this one, early-filters-and-pagination.md, groupby-aggregate-performance.md) are structured the same way: a mechanism, then the plan field that proves it fired. There is a case for phase 2 promoting a single `plan-field:` namespace or a consistent `index:*-plan-field` family rather than minting them one page at a time - the corpus currently has index:covers-plan-field and, after this wave, index:filter-covers-plan-field, index:index-keys-plan-field, index:index-conditions-plan-field, index:index-key-plan-expression and index:index-group-aggs-plan-field, all discovered the same way.
cross_product_finding: Example 6 of this Capella page instructs the reader to 'insert the following documents into the default collection in the default scope in the `travel-sample` bucket' and then creates an index on `` `travel-sample` `` at the bucket level, while every other example on the page uses collection-level keyspaces (`hotel`, `landmark`) under an assumed inventory scope. That is a pre-collections example that survived the 7.0 keyspace change and the Capella re-edit, and it contradicts the sibling pages in this batch, which all open with 'you must set the query context to the `inventory` scope'. This page has no query-context instruction at all, so Examples 1-5 cannot be run as written without one. Worth a docs issue, but it is phase 2's call, not mine.
